Tests all 16,383 height-two paths at n=1..14 by the literal factor predicate against truncated closure, verifies the transported statistics and reproduces counts 1,2,3,5,7,12,16,27,37,58,80,131,171,277. At g=1..7 it finds 0,1,2,4,9,17,31 just below saturation versus stabilized counts 1,2,4,7,12,23,39.
correctness.rationale: For 0 as the up-step, Z(j)=(j+H(j))/2. The original factor inequalities are therefore exactly H(a+ℓ)≤H(a)+H(ℓ), including the zero-length and full-length boundaries. At height at most two all odd vertices have height one, and each internal even vertex independently has height zero or two. An inequality can fail only when a=2i and ℓ=2k both refer to zero heights but i+k refers to a lifted internal vertex. Thus the return indices together with 0 are closed under all sums strictly below n, and adjoining the full tail from n onward yields precisely the numerical semigroups of conductor at most n. Its inverse prescribes the even heights. Each gap lifts one even vertex; the n odd vertices give the remaining height sum, so the area is n+2g. The endpoint index n is always a return, ensuring the multiplicity formula even without internal returns, and the last lifted index gives the conductor, with zero in the no-gap case. For a positive genus semigroup with largest gap F, the involution i↦F−i sends nongaps in [0,F] injectively to gaps, proving c≤2g even if there is a central fixed point. The semigroup generated by 2 and 2g+1 has the g odd gaps through 2g−1, attaining c=2g and proving the strict inequality at n=2g−1. Genus zero gives one word at every n≥1.
residual_risks: The finite tests do not prove the all-length result. The OEIS series is a total count indexed by n−1, not the total genus-g semigroup count at every semilength.

value.rationale: The result completely classifies a naturally constrained Dyck word language by a well-studied additive object. It translates an all-factors inequality into closure on return indices and makes the area distribution, first-return statistic, and sharp onset of genus-count saturation interpretable via a single inverse map. This is useful even though the numerical sequence and the conductor inequality were known.
residual_risks: The result does not enumerate unrestricted prefix-normal Dyck words or give a new general formula for the genus counts.
